steps.label: Do Now: Parity Checks (1 of 3)
steps.content:
Do Now: Parity Checks (1 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the printer need its data checked at all?Show the answer

Interference can change bits on the way. A changed bit could print the wrong thing.

From 2.2 L1 and L2. Part (a): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2026, Question 4(b)(i). An odd parity byte check is used to check for errors in data that is transmitted from a computer to a printer. There is an error in the data after transmission. This error is not detected by the parity byte check.

Total: 3 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: parity byte and parity block

steps.text: Parity byte. A different byte, sent with even parity. Count the 1s.
steps.visual:
01101001
1s sent: 4. Even, so it matches even parity.

steps.text: On the way, two bits change. Bit 2 goes from 1 to 0. Bit 7 goes from 0 to 1.
steps.visual: 01101001 → 00101011

steps.text: The receiver counts the 1s that arrived.
steps.visual:
00101011
1s that arrived: 4

steps.text: Think: the receiver only sees the count. What does it see here? What does it decide? Now use the same idea for odd parity in part (a).
Parity block. A different block, even parity. One bit changed. First check every row.
steps.visual:
P1234

Byte 211111
Byte 300110

Byte 2 has five 1s: odd

Column 2 has three 1s: odd

steps.label: Do Now: Checksum and Echo Check (2 of 3)
steps.content:
Do Now: Checksum and Echo Check (2 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy check data sent 30 kilometres?Show the answer

A long cable picks up more interference, so bits are more likely to change.

From 2.2 L2 and L3. Part (a): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2021, Question 1(d)(iii). Data about the final score for a match is transmitted to a central computer 30 kilometres away. The data transmission uses checksums.

Total: 5 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: checksum and echo check

steps.text: Describe a check. A similar question: describe how a parity check detects errors. Answer in the order things happen.
Before sending: the sender adds a parity bit so the number of 1s is odd or even.
steps.visual: Before sending→After arriving→Decide

steps.text: After arriving: the receiver counts the 1s in the byte that arrived.
steps.visual: Before sending→After arriving→Decide

steps.text: Decide: the count does not fit the parity, so there is an error. One point for each step.
steps.visual: Before sending→After arriving→Decide

steps.text: For part (a), follow these three steps for a checksum: what happens before sending, after arriving, and how the receiver decides.
Why twice? A different case: a teacher marks a test, and a second teacher marks it again. Why do it twice?
One mark on its own tells you nothing. Put the two side by side: now you can see something went wrong. Use this idea for part (b).
Echo check. A different case: you post a letter to a friend. Your friend posts a photocopy of it back to you. The photocopy has a smudge.
steps.visual:
Your letter: clean
Photocopy back: smudge

steps.text: The smudge could come from the trip to your friend, or from the trip back to you. You hold two things: your letter and the photocopy.
Think: what would you need to look at to know which trip made the smudge? Do you have it? Use this idea for part (c).

Do Now: ARQ (3 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy use a parity check AND ARQ together?Show the answer

The parity check finds the error. ARQ makes sure the data is sent again.

From 2.2 L1 to L3. Part (a): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2024, Question 9(b)(ii). A company checks data for errors after transmission. The error detection system uses an odd parity check and a positive automatic repeat query (ARQ).

Total: 4 marks

steps.label: Check Digits
steps.content:
2.2 Methods of Error Detection

Check Digits

Year 10

  • Today: mistakes when a person types a number, or a machine scans one, and how a check digit finds them.
  • You already know: parity checks, checksums, echo checks and ARQ. They find errors when data is sent.
Think → Pair → ShareA shop worker types a product number and presses one wrong key. Why is that a problem? Could a parity check find it?Show the answer

The wrong number is the data. A parity check only checks that data arrives the same as it was sent, so it would not find it. We need a different check.

steps.label: Data Entry Errors
steps.content:
Data Entry Errors

Think → Pair → SharePredict: Ana should type 69321. She types 69821. Ben types 96321. What went wrong each time?Show the worked answer

Ana typed one digit wrong: 3 became 8.

Ben swapped two digits: 6 and 9 changed places.

The computer cannot see the number they meant. These are data entry errors.

  • Data entry: a person types a number, or a scanner reads one.
  • Two common errors: one digit wrong, or two digits swapped.
  • The error happens before the data is sent, so a parity check or checksum cannot see it.
Should be
69321
Ana typed
69821
Ben typed
96321

steps.label: The Check Digit
steps.content:
The Check Digit

Think → Pair → SharePredict: the last digit of 512435 was worked out from the first five digits. Ben types 512485. How could the computer notice?Show the worked answer

It works out the last digit again from the first five digits it got. The answer will not match the 5 that was typed, so there is an error.

  • A check digit is an extra digit at the end of a number.
  • It is calculated from the other digits, using an algorithm.
  • When the number is entered, the computer calculates it again and compares.
  • They match: accepted. Different: an error, so the number is entered again.
  • Used in ISBN numbers on books, and in bar codes on products.
512435

the last digit is the check digit

steps.label: Exam Question: What a Check Digit Is For
steps.content:
Exam Question: What a Check Digit Is For

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the mark scheme want the word "calculated"?Show the answer

The check digit is not chosen at random. It is worked out from the other digits, so the computer can work it out again.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/23, June 2026, Question 3(b). Explain the purpose of a check digit and give an example of where it could be used.

Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Method 1: Add the Digits
steps.content:
Method 1: Add the Digits

Think → Pair → SharePredict: add up the digits of 51243. Divide the total by 10. What is the remainder?Show the worked answer

5 + 1 + 2 + 4 + 3 = 15. 15 divided by 10 is 1, remainder 5.

So the check digit is 5, and the full number is 512435.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/23, November 2022, Question 3. The check digit is calculated by adding up the first five digits, dividing by 10 and taking the remainder.

  • Step 1: add up the digits.
  • Step 2: divide the total by 10.
  • Step 3: the remainder is the check digit.
  • The remainder is always 0 to 9: one digit.
StepWorking
15 + 1 + 2 + 4 + 3 = 15
215 ÷ 10 = 1 remainder 5
3check digit = 5
512435

A wrong number looks just like a right one. Only the calculation shows it.

steps.label: Compare: One Wrong Digit and Two Swapped
steps.content:
Compare: One Wrong Digit and Two Swapped

Think → Pair → ShareThe right number is 372541. Two people type it wrongly. Predict: does Method 1 find both errors?Show the answer

It finds the wrong digit: the total changes, so the remainder changes.

It does not find the swap: the same digits give the same total, in any order.

One digit typed wrong

378541

3 + 7 + 8 + 5 + 4 = 27
remainder 7. Typed check digit: 1.
Different: the error is found.

Two digits swapped

327541

3 + 2 + 7 + 5 + 4 = 21
remainder 1. Typed check digit: 1.
They match: the error is NOT found.

  • Adding the digits finds one wrong digit.
  • It misses two digits swapped: the total stays the same.

steps.label: Method 2: Multiply by Position
steps.content:
Method 2: Multiply by Position

Think → Pair → SharePredict: swap the first two digits, 03475. With Method 2, does the check digit change?Show the worked answer

Yes. 0 × 1 + 3 × 2 + 4 × 3 + 7 × 4 + 5 × 5 = 71. MOD(71, 11) = 5, not 2.

Each digit is multiplied by a different number, so a swap changes the total. The swap is found.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/21, November 2025, Question 6. The check digit for a 5-digit number:

  • Multiply each digit by its position (the first digit is position 1).
  • Add the results: the total.
  • MOD(Total, 11) is the remainder after dividing by 11.
  • If the result is 10, the check digit is X.
Digit30475
Position12345
Digit × position30122825

3 + 0 + 12 + 28 + 25 = 68
68 = 6 × 11 + 2, so MOD(68, 11) = 2

steps.label: Check: When It Does Not Match
steps.content:
Check: When It Does Not Match

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can a check digit not correct the error?Show the answer

It only tells the computer the number is wrong, not which digit is wrong.

Choose one answer for each.

items.prompt: A bar code is scanned. The computer calculates the check digit again, and it does not match. What happens?
options: The computer corrects the wrong digit
The data is sent again down the cable
The bar code is rejected and scanned again
The check digit is changed to match
items.explain: A check digit only shows THAT there is an error. It cannot show which digit is wrong, so the number is entered or scanned again.

items.prompt: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2023, Question 5(b). Some error detection methods use a calculated value to check for errors. Which error detection method does NOT use a calculated value to check for errors?
items.explain: An echo check sends a copy of the data back and compares. Nothing is calculated.

Think → Pair → ShareA bar code is scanned at a till. Then the price is sent to the stock computer. Which check fits each step? Why?Show the answer

Scanning is data entry: a check digit finds a bad scan.

Sending to the stock computer is transmission: a parity check, checksum, echo check or ARQ finds bits changed on the way.

steps.label: Exam Question: The Bar Code Scanner
steps.content:
Exam Question: The Bar Code Scanner

Think → Pair → ShareThis has 4 marks. What happens before the scan, and what happens after it?Show the answer

Before: the check digit is calculated and added. After: it is calculated again and the two are compared.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2024, Question 5. A barcode scanning system uses a check digit to check for errors in data on input.

items.prompt: (a) Explain how the barcode scanning system operates to check for errors. [4]
items.modelAnswer: Any four: a check digit is calculated from the barcode data; using an algorithm (for example, modulo 11); and added to the barcode; when the barcode is scanned the check digit is recalculated; using the same algorithm; if the check digits do not match, an error has occurred when scanning the barcode (if they match, no error has occurred).
